title: Demo security review prep (enterprise) — artifacts + Q&A (data retention/residency)
content:
Purpose
- This doc is a prep sheet for AE/SE-led enterprise security review calls that happen after (or alongside) the standard product demo.
- Goal: be crisp, consistent, and safe. Keep the call moving by showing the right artifacts, avoiding anything that creates risk/confusion, and answering data retention/residency questions in plain language.

Audience
- Security reviewer / GRC
- IT / Identity owner
- Infra/Platform owner (VPC + network questions)
- Procurement/legal sometimes joins late (keep them out of rabbit holes; offer follow-up packet)

Non-negotiables (demo hygiene)
- Demo tenant contains synthetic data only. No customer identifiers, no real prompts, no real payload logs.
- Never screenshare internal tools that are not approved for external audiences (Slack, internal dashboards, Jira/Linear, raw logs, on-call tooling).
- If asked for compliance docs (SOC 2 report, pen test letter, DPA), do not improvise. Offer the standard path: “We can share under NDA via secure channel; I’ll coordinate with our security team.”

What to show (safe artifacts)
1) Security overview (slides or verbal)
- High-level shared responsibility: what Redwood secures vs what the customer controls.
- Deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, Private (VPC/on-prem) — emphasize same API + operational controls, different isolation boundaries.

2) Console: identity & access controls (only if enabled in demo environment)
- RBAC: show roles, least-privilege approach (viewer vs admin) and how access is scoped to org/project.
- SSO/SAML (screenshots preferred unless we have stable staging IdP): show SSO configuration page and explain typical integration (Okta/AzureAD).

3) Audit logs (screenshots preferred)
- Show sample audit events for:
  - API key creation/rotation
  - Role changes
  - SSO login / policy updates
- Explain what’s captured, searchable fields, and export options (if applicable).

4) Data controls summary
- Retention controls: what data is stored by default, what can be configured/limited, and how deletion works.
- Encryption: in transit + at rest, and KMS/HSM integration story for Private deployments.

5) Private/VPC architecture narrative (diagram + talk track)
- Keep it architectural: control plane vs data plane, customer-managed networking, how traffic routes.
- Emphasize that Private deploys keep inference traffic and artifacts within the customer’s environment boundary (VPC/on-prem), with customer-owned network controls.

What NOT to show (avoid / common pitfalls)
- Raw request/response payload logs (even if synthetic). Most reviewers interpret “we can see payloads” as a red flag.
- Any internal-only views that reveal:
  - other tenants/projects (risk of implied multi-tenant data exposure)
  - capacity dashboards by customer name
  - internal incident tooling / pages
- Live toggling settings that can destabilize the demo tenant (quota/rate limit pages, model catalog admin pages, routing policy editors unless specifically rehearsed).
- “Trust me” performance screenshots with unapproved numbers. Use the approved benchmark snippets only (Soojin/Marketing maintains what’s safe).

Default security story (60–90 seconds)
- “Redwood is built to run LLM inference with production reliability and enterprise controls across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. We support strong identity controls (SSO/SAML + RBAC), audit logging for administrative actions, encryption in transit/at rest, and configurable data retention. For regulated workloads, Private/VPC deployment keeps traffic within your network boundary while preserving the same API and operational tooling.”

Key Q&A (use these exact frames)

1) Data retention — what do you store?
Answer frame:
- “We separate (a) inference content and (b) operational telemetry.”
- “By default, we retain only what’s required to operate the service and provide observability; content retention is configurable based on plan/deployment mode.”
- “For Private/VPC deployments, you control the environment and retention policies within your infrastructure boundary.”
Follow-ups to clarify (ask before answering details):
- “Are you asking about prompt/response content, embeddings vectors, or just operational logs?”
- “Do you have a specific retention requirement (e.g., 0 days, 7 days, 30 days)?”
What to offer (safe):
- “We can align retention to your requirements and document it in the MSA/DPA / security addendum as needed.”
Avoid:
- Don’t state a specific number of days unless you have the current policy in front of you or Security confirms.

2) Data residency — where is data processed and stored?
Answer frame:
- “Residency is about (a) where inference is executed and (b) where any stored artifacts/telemetry live.”
- “We can run inference in specific regions depending on your deployment choice and region availability.”
- “For strict residency needs, Private/VPC is the cleanest option because execution stays within your VPC/on-prem footprint.”
Qualifying questions:
- “Is your requirement ‘EU-only processing,’ ‘EU-only storage,’ or both?”
- “Do you need residency for request content, or also for operational telemetry and audit logs?”
Avoid:
- Don’t promise specific region coverage or “no cross-border transfer” language without the formal security package.

3) Do you train on customer data?
Answer frame:
- “No. We do not train foundation models on customer prompts/responses.”
- “We use data only as needed to operate the service and to provide product features customers enable (e.g., evals you configure), subject to contract.”
Avoid:
- Don’t volunteer internal R&D details; keep it contractual/operational.

4) Who has access to our data? (internal access controls)
Answer frame:
- “Access is limited by role-based controls and audited. Administrative actions are logged.”
- “Support access follows an approved process; for Private/VPC, you can constrain access further via your network controls.”
If pressed:
- Offer follow-up with Security for details on support access workflow and auditing.

5) Encryption / key management
Answer frame:
- “Encryption in transit (TLS) and at rest. For enterprise deployments we support integrations with customer key management (KMS/HSM) depending on deployment mode.”
- “We can share exact implementation details in the security packet.”
Avoid:
- Don’t cite specific ciphers, key rotation cadence, or vendor names unless you’re reading from the current security FAQ.

6) Incident response / breach notification
Answer frame:
- “We have an incident response program and defined escalation paths. We can share our standard incident notification terms and security processes under NDA.”
Avoid:
- Don’t commit to custom timelines on the call.

Call flow (recommended)
0–3 min: confirm goal + who’s in the room
- “What do you need to be true to move forward—SSO, audit logs, retention, residency, or private deployment controls?”
3–10 min: identity + audit logs (highest signal)
10–18 min: data retention/residency (use Q&A frames)
18–25 min: Private/VPC architecture narrative + what’s required from customer side
25–30 min: next steps + offer security packet + schedule follow-up deep dive (if needed)

Screenshare plan (if doing any live Console tour)
- Use a clean browser profile (no extensions, no bookmarks).
- Use a dedicated “Security Review” project/org in demo tenant (pre-created) so there’s no navigation confusion.
- Keep time range filters set (avoid empty graphs / awkward states).
- Have backup screenshots ready in a separate folder in case Console is slow.

Artifacts checklist to have open BEFORE the call
- Demo security FAQ (short answers + links)
- Private/VPC architecture diagram (approved)
- Audit log screenshots (approved + redacted)
- SSO/SAML screenshot set (approved)
- One-slide “data retention vs telemetry” explainer
- Escalation list (who to pull in)

Escalation / SMEs (internal)
- Security/GRC: Naomi Feldman (product advisor), Marcus Lin (security eng reviewer)
- Auth/SSO/RBAC: Ethan Park
- Demo tenant + runbooks: Markus Klein
- Private architecture talk track: Simran Kaur

Common traps + exact deflections
- Trap: Reviewer asks for SOC 2 Type II report live
  - “We can share the SOC 2 report under NDA via our secure process. If you tell me your timeline, we’ll get it to you today/tomorrow.”
- Trap: Reviewer asks “Do you log prompts?”
  - “We can configure how content is handled; operational telemetry is separate. Let’s define which content, if any, you need retained for debugging, and we’ll align to that requirement and document it.”
- Trap: Reviewer wants definitive residency statement without scoping
  - “Residency depends on whether the requirement is processing vs storage and which deployment mode you choose. If you confirm your requirement, we’ll map it to Hosted/Dedicated/Private options and provide the formal answer in writing.”

Notes from recent calls (patterns)
- HelioHealth: main blockers were residency + retention clarity; they interpreted ‘observability’ as ‘we store content.’ We need to lead with the separation between content vs telemetry.
- Northstar Payments: procurement joined late; they cared more about audit trails + incident response wording than the technical details. Keep the call structured; offer a follow-up packet.
